Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 6184 -1971 

Indian Standard 

DIMENSIONS FOR 
FURNITURE MIRRORS 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institu- 
tion on 30 July 1971, after the draft finalized by the Furniture Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 

0.2 The use of mirrors on domestic furniture has been popular for a long 
time in the past but the approach of the most of the furniture manufactu- 
rers towards mounting the mirrors has been rather arbitrary with the 
result that users have been using the mirrors which are mounted at heights 
either too high or too low. In order to make the best use of the 
commercial sizes of mirrors available, an attempt has been made to 
rationalize the mounting heights of the mirrors fixed to articles of 
furniture, 

0.3 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to 
international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing 
in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field 
in this country. 

0.4 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on furniture. 

0.5 Fori:he purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accord- 
ance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard. 



1, SCOPE 

1.1 This standard refers to domestic furniture and fixes the functional 
dimensions of mirrors fixed to articles of furniture. 

Note 1 — This standard does not apply to mirrors for decorative purposes ( rear walls 
of cupboards and shelves, cabinets, etc). 

Note 2 — This standard does not fix the shape of the mirror. 



♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised), 

3 



IS j 6184 -1971 



2. MATERIAL 

2.1 The furniture mirrors shall comply with the requirements laid down in 
IS: 3438-1965*. 

3. DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The dimensions of full length mirrors shall be as given in Fig. 1 and 
of half length mirrors as given in Fig. 2. Figures 3 and 4 show the 
dimensions of mirrors used in sitting posture. Figure 3 fixes the dimen- 
sions for the vertical position and Fig. 4 fixes the dimensions for inclined 
position. 

4. WIDTH 

4.1 The width of the individual mirrors in folding mirrors shall not be less 
than 200 mm*

5. DESIGN 

5.1 The design of articles of furniture with mirrors with functional 
dimensions as given in this standard shall be in conformity with the 
technical documents on furniture items.
